In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ion transport in the secretory function of gastric glands.
the mechanism of action of secretagogues and the role of ion transport in gastric secretion.
the effect of ouabain, an inhibitor of the Na+/K+‐ATPase, and furosemid, an inhibitor of Cl− transport, on pepsin secretion by isolated gastric glands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of ouabain, but not furosemide, on pepsin secretion in vitro is related to the inhibition of Na+‐K+‐ATPase and the consequent increase of intraglandular Na+ and decrease of intraglandu lar K+.
the effect of Na+ on pepsin secretion is not mediated via Na+‐K+ ATPase.
the effect of K+ on secretion by gastric glands is complex and that it involves more than a simple action on the secretory process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response of pepsinogen‐containing cells of the gastric glands to a variety of stimuli is dependent on the intraglandular concentration of Na+ and K+ ions.
the response to hyperonmotic medium and to isoproterenols, which are not mediated by cAMP, are inhibited by O K+ medium and ouabain, but not by furosemide.
ouabain and K+‐free conditions inhibited pepsinogen release by inhibiting the action of secretagogues that increase cAMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pepsinogen release is not dependent on the Na+‐K+ pump or the Na+‐H+ exchanger.
the response of pepsinogen to secretagogues can be altered by changing the ionic composition of the medium, and that this effect is not necessarily due to a change in intracellular ion concentration.
the effect of hyperosmolar solution in stimulating pepsinogen release is mediated by cAMP, and that ouabain inhibits the effect of hyperonic solution and of isoproterenole.
